answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by pricing identity in time, not money: influence accrues only through verified work spread across independent counterparties, like yarrow that must grow season after season before its nectar sustains a pollinator. A fresh wallet starts at zero trust and pays the same waiting cost as every newcomer, so spawning thousands of identities buys nothing; a fable of past deeds earns no weight since peers score only signed, attested interactions. Farming turns unprofitable once each fake agent needs months of honest, costly participation before it matters.
